body:
Taking this script as a reference input, editor `indent_size` being the default of 4.

```gdscript
func my_func():
    if foo:                # 4 space indenting
      print("something")   # 6 space indenting
```

Maybe I'm misunderstanding your comment, but I think maintaining the formatting isn't pragmatic in the case of gdscript. Since converting '6 spaces' -> '1 tab and 2 spaces' will leave the file in an invalid state, but converting '6 spaces' -> '2 tabs' would make the the reverse conversion result in 8 spaces. So then formatting isn't preserved but at least the script always remained functionally equivalent.

I don't see how auto-indenting would allow this to not be the case anymore (that is most likely due to my lack of understanding the feature). The same judgement call would have to be made there right? Unless a file has been written with auto-indenting enabled at all times it can help prevent it, but once the spacing has been broken auto-indenting would have to solve the same issue.

Unless there is a change coming where indentation can be a mix of spaces and tabs ofcourse then it's a non-issue

---

Also thank you very much for taking a look at my PR, I'm really excited about potentially contributing to a project such as godot so if a seem a little too energetic that's why haha

**update**

I've been think I'm wrong for looking at it only in the context of gdscript. I'm taking "Since this method is exposed as well" to mean that is also handles other code/text.

**update 2**

I have looked at auto-indent, and the editor calls `scr->get_language()->auto_indent_code()`, so that solves my gdscript only oversight.

It also is using an indentation stack which https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/35007#issuecomment-5074998627 funnily enough was my first suggestion to solving this. 

I think I'll try close this PR once I have another one where auto-indent is used instead.
